analysis.session_summary: The tape was dominated by JPY strength (USD/JPY -56.3 pips, CHF/JPY -159.5 pips) and CHF weakness (USD/CHF +38.9 pips, EUR/CHF +28.8 pips), while AUD and NZD firmed against USD (+9.1 and +11.6 pips). US CPI m/m (0.3% vs 0.2%) and UoM sentiment (47.8 vs 51.0) were measured muted at the basket level, with own-currency impulses of 0.008% and 0.029%, but high-beta USD pairs showed large z-score responses. Risk closed mixed: SPX +0.837% while VIX +3.286%; Brent fell 1.602%. USD/CAD rose 45.9 pips into upcoming Canadian CPI, keeping CAD weakest alongside CHF.

themes.evidence: JPY mean strength 0.462; USD/JPY -56.3 pips; CHF/JPY -159.5 pips (-0.84%).
CHF mean strength -0.501; USD/CHF +38.9 pips; EUR/CHF +28.8; AUD/CHF +35.3; NZD/CHF +31.9.

themes.theme: Commodity/risk FX firmer despite VIX rise

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped around 1.1600: a -21.5 pip NY morning down leg from 08:00 to 13:45 was mostly retraced by a +22.7 pip up leg from 13:45 to 16:45, leaving only -19.8 pips on the day.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY's 01:30-to-18:45 down leg of -85.3 pips dominated, with Core CPI contributing -24.1 pips (28% of the move); the pair closed -56.3 pips at 153.711.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD traded in a 52.7-pip range and finished nearly flat (-0.3 pips), with a UK GDP-driven +27.0 pip up leg offset by a UoM-driven -8.8 pip late dip.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF built +19.7, -15.0, +31.0, -15.7, +19.2 pips legs to close +38.9 pips, reflecting steady CHF weakness despite intraday pullbacks.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD's 19:00-17:00 +66.3 pip grind up was only partly retraced by -17.2 pips into the close, leaving +45.9 pips at 1.38635.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD had an initial -12.6 pip dip, then a 05:15-14:45 +33.0 pip up leg, but finished only +9.1 pips after a -9.8 pip late fade.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD's 23:45-08:00 +40.2 pip surge set the tone, but the 08:00-18:45 -17.2 pip fade left it +11.6 pips at 0.58164.

polarity_reads.read: Measured muted at 0.008% basket impulse, but top movers showed USD strength (EUR/USD -14.3 pips, GBP/USD -19.1, USD/CHF +12.9); this implies limited broad USD impulse with high-beta pairs doing most of the adjustment.
Normal polarity: 0.4% vs 0.0% beat gave GBP +0.075%, confirming expected GBP strength; top movers EUR/GBP -2.4 pips and GBP/USD +3.7 pips.
Measured muted at 0.018% basket impulse; no EUR follow-through, with top movers concentrated in EM/USD rather than EUR crosses.

Measured muted at 0.029% basket impulse despite the 47.8 vs 51.0 miss; high-beta EM pairs like USD/MXN +122.0 pips and USD/ZAR +174.8 pips moved, indicating the USD response was concentrated in EM/commodity crosses rather than a broad dollar bid.
Measured muted at -0.013% basket impulse; CHF/JPY -6.4 pips was the top mover, suggesting the day's CHF weakness was flow-driven rather than event-driven.

scenarios.name: JPY bid extends, CHF weakness continues
scenarios.thesis: The tape's strongest bias (JPY strength 0.462, CHF strength -0.501) carries into the next window; USD/JPY remains offered while USD/CHF stays bid.
triggers: CHF crosses extend above current levels
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY recovers back through 153.711 and USD/CHF gives up its 38.9-pip day gain.

pair_paths.rationale: Matches the measured session close gain.

scenarios.name: Mean reversion/profit-taking ahead of CAD CPI
scenarios.thesis: After USD/CAD's +66.3 pip up leg and stretched CHF crosses, profit-taking may dominate into the CAD CPI release, pulling USD/CAD back and stabilizing USD/JPY.
triggers: CAD CPI at 14:30 is not weaker than forecast
scenarios.invalidation: USD/CAD breaks above 1.38635 and holds above the 19:00-17:00 +66.3 pip up leg.

scenarios.name: USD catches a fresh bid / CAD CPI weak
scenarios.thesis: A weak Canadian CPI or risk-off headline could lift USD against CAD and EUR, reversing part of the late USD/CAD pullback.
triggers: Median CPI y/y below 2.0% or trimmed below 1.9%
scenarios.invalidation: USD/CAD unable to hold above 1.38635, EUR/USD reclaims 1.15996 close.

pair_paths.rationale: Matches the session gain on CAD weakness.

risks.why_it_matters: USD/CAD has a 70.5-pip range and is already up 45.9 pips; a weak print could extend the move, while a firm print could unwind it.
risks.watch: CPI m/m forecast -0.1% vs previous 0.5%; median/trimmed at 2.0%/1.9%.

risks.why_it_matters: SPX +0.837% with VIX +3.286% hints at hedged risk demand; a sustained VIX rise could hit high-beta FX.
CHF mean strength -0.501% and CHF/JPY -159.5 pips leave crosses vulnerable to squeeze; SNB Schlegel was measured muted.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Next window brings ECB President Lagarde at 10:00 EUR and a high-impact CAD CPI block at 14:30 (headline forecast -0.1% m/m vs previous 0.5%; median 2.0%, trimmed 1.9%). CAD and EUR crosses can reprice from this, especially after USD/CAD +45.9 pips today.
